subject: GPU pool bump plan + autoscale exception for noisy canary
messages:
From: Satya Rao <satya@acme-ai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@acme-ai.com
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot needs + possible capacity bump (Acme AI)

Hi Olga and team —

Quick context: the Acme pilot has two parallel experiments this week (semantic search and multi-turn summarization). The search job is much noisier than expected and is spiking GPU usage during short bursts (10–30s) even though average QPS is within the pilot target. We could probably absorb this with autoscale, but procurement is asking if we can guarantee capacity during their show-and-tell on Friday.

Can Redwood carve a temporary bump or an exception to the autoscale policy for the pilot window (Aug 6–8)? They want a short, cheap way to avoid throttling for 2–3 live demos.

Thanks,
Satya
Head of Product, Acme AI

---
Attachments: none
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Pilot needs + possible capacity bump (Acme AI)

Satya —

Thanks for the heads-up. Short answer: we can provide a temporary dedicated buffer but need to align on three things before I commit:

1) Exact peak slot count and times (so ops can pin capacity instead of relying on autoscale).
2) Pricing for the temporary carve (we can do a short-term uplift vs. a reserved window).
3) An operational rollback plan so we don't impact other customers if usage keeps spiking.

Kimberly, can you take point on commercial terms? Jonas / Dev — please advise on operational feasibility and whether we need a policy exemption for autoscale during a demo window.

Olga
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Satya Rao <satya@acme-ai.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot needs + possible capacity bump (Acme AI)

On Mon, Aug 02, 2026 at 10:05 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Kimberly, can you take point on commercial terms? Jonas / Dev — please advise on operational feasibility and whether we need a policy exemption for autoscale during a demo window.

We can do a temporary carve as a short-lived "burst reservation" attached to Acme's pilot. Operational notes:

- We can pin an extra 8 A100-equivalent slots in us-west-2 for the window Aug 6 08:00–Aug 8 20:00 PDT.
- That will remove those slots from autoscale pools (explicit carve) and route Acme traffic to the pinned pool.
- Fallback: if utilization still exceeds pinned capacity, the router can failover to hosted fallbacks (lower-tier model variant) — requires Acme sign-off.
- Risk: this reduces available burst capacity for other pilots during the window.

Do we need a formal autoscale policy exception? Technically yes — our autoscale policy forbids manual pinning outside reserved contracts without a documented exception. I can kick off the exception doc but need an approval chain (Product -> Ops -> Sales exec).

I'll attach a rough capacity plan (numbers below) and a short runbook for ops.

Jonas
Senior Infra Ops

Subject: Re: Pilot needs + possible capacity bump (Acme AI)

Thanks — I'll handle the commercial side. A few quick proposals:

- Option A (low friction): 3-day burst add-on at a flat incremental fee (30% uplift on pilot committed rate). Fast approval (I can sign).
- Option B (preferred for enterprise): a short-term reserved window (billable as reserved capacity prorated for the 72 hours). Requires commercial sign-off & PO.
- Option C (no-cost escalation): provide the carve on us once if Acme pushes the demo team to consolidate load patterns (not sustainable but sometimes used as a goodwill).

Satya — which option makes procurement and leadership comfortable for Friday's demo? If they pick A, I can issue an order today and we can request the autoscale exception doc to follow.

Kimberly
